claims.text: The initial material and comparator are unchanged bulk HfNbTaTiZr.
Oxygen vacancies can be introduced into bulk HfNbTaTiZr as a single intervention.
Introducing oxygen vacancies into HfNbTaTiZr produces lattice distortions.
Increased phonon scattering caused by lattice distortion lowers lattice thermal conductivity.
Oxygen-vacancy-containing bulk HfNbTaTiZr will have lower lattice thermal conductivity than unchanged bulk HfNbTaTiZr.
The predicted reduction applies from approximately 0 to 200 K.
The magnitude of the lattice-thermal-conductivity reduction is unknown.
A comparison of samples with and without oxygen vacancies over 0–200 K is proposed as the experimental control design.
Thermal conductivity and lattice parameter are the proposed measurements.
Failure to observe lower lattice thermal conductivity after the intervention would falsify the hypothesis.

contradictions.description: The starting material is specified only as nominal HfNbTaTiZr, with no oxygen-bearing sublattice, yet the intervention is described as introducing oxygen vacancies. A vacancy requires pre-existing oxygen sites or a prior oxygen-addition step, neither of which is specified.

The measurements list only overall thermal conductivity and lattice parameter, whereas the falsification rule requires determining lattice thermal conductivity specifically. No electrical-resistivity or other electronic-transport measurement is included to separate lattice and electronic contributions.
